To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
exposure to appetitive food cues activates reward and attention networks in the human brain.

1) The brain responds differently to food stimuli depending on whether the food stimuli is a picture of a food item, the smell of a food item (odourant), or the actual food item (taste); 2) The brain responds to food stimuli differently depending on the type of food stimuli (e.g. high-fat vs. high-carbohydrate foods) and whether the food stimuli has a high or low caloric value.
exposure to appetitive food cues (e.g. food images) markedly activates the human reward circuitry, which is composed of the ventral tegmental area and nucleus accumbens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of food on the brain.
the neural basis of food motivation and food intake.
the effects of food cues on brain activity in healthy subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain is a highly sensitive organ to food stimuli, and that this sensitivity is related to the hedonic value of food.
the human brain is highly sensitive to the presence of food and that this sensitivity can be modulated by hunger and satiety, and that it is influenced by the type and amount of food.
the consumption of a meal, in particular of high fat and/or high carbohydrate food, activates the reward system of the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a strong relationship between the activation of the reward circuitry and the subjective experience of hunger.
we have shown that exposure to appetitive food cues (e.g. food images) activates the human brain and that this brain activation is associated with food intake.
the brain is not just a machine, but also a very sensitive and complex organ.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain’s response to food is highly sensitive to the context in which food is presented and the state of the body.
the brain is very sensitive to food cues.
food stimuli activate a network of regions in the brain that are involved in reward, emotion, and cognition.
